speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history. To better understand your new movement disorder, have you noticed any tremors, stiffness, or involuntary movements, and do these symptoms appear when you are at rest or during activity?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is excellent news regarding your psychiatric improvement. However, the timing of your new movement symptoms two months after starting risperidone suggests a medication side effect; can you describe exactly what those movements look like, such as rhythmic shaking, muscle tightness, or repetitive writhing motions?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Extrapyramidal Symptoms (Akathisia) secondary to Risperidone. The patient's description of inner restlessness, fidgeting, and an inability to remain still is classic for this side effect; the mention of pneumonia appears to be a miscommunication or misunderstanding. We should discontinue or switch the antipsychotic medication.
